chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Starting in New York and its heyday
summary: He came to New York after leaving Chicago and has been there since; Rasch calls it the center of everything and he says he was on his way in the 1940s.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you start in music, writing music?
I don't really know. I just did.
You were in New York City though.
Yes. I came to New York, when I left home, in Chicago, and I've been in New York ever since.
Boy, you must have seen a lot of changes in New York City, I bet.
Oh, definitely so -- but I like it all, somehow.
New York City was some kind of beautiful place many years ago.
They call it the Paris of the world.

Both culturally and musically, it was the place to be, that was the place everything was happening, it was the place where the top people got their starts, it was just a paradise of beginnings. Show me that drawing of New York City again, I don't know what year it was -- 30's or 40's, and I just couldn't believe it was the center for so much. It was the era that you became popular, though.
Yes, it sure was -- the 40's, yes sir. I was on my way.
